notes.summary: Actual geometric finite pullback is proved on source PRIMARY blowups; full positive C/D descent uses qualified G331. Noninjective maps descend to their exact image.
notes.detailedSummary: The actual source blowup is closed in finite base change. Regular effective Cartier presentations and contracted-curve degrees prove geometric core pullback on every nonempty source component. Completed class descent retains all fibres and supports. No extension from a quotient image to the original target is inferred.
notes.text:
Use the entire qualified G331 and G345, preserving all mandatory annotations, ledgers and scopes. Let R be excellent reduced local, a a proper primary ideal, and X_R the FULL centred semivaluation section v(a)=1. Every prime support strictly below the closed point is retained. For a reduced finite R-algebra B, X_B is the disjoint union of sections at its closed centres, normalized by aB. Zero-dimensional centres have empty boundary; positive lower-dimensional centres remain.

C denotes G331's independently geometric continuous cone; D consists of actual infima of nonempty decreasing C-nets. G331 proves comparison with the uniform ideal cone and its stated decreasing completion. This comparison is used as a theorem, not as the definition of geometric positivity. G345 supplies independently positive bounded products on D, with PRIMARY models, ordinary OPEN locality, prescribed-D-limit decreasing-net continuity and exact BFJ smooth scope. Neither grant supplies general envelopes or energy.

For a primary base ideal I, degreewise multiplication gives a surjection Rees_R(I) tensor_R B -> Rees_B(IB), because the degree-r image is I^r B=(IB)^r. Taking relative Proj embeds the ACTUAL source blowup Bl_(IB)(B) as a closed subscheme of Spec(B) times_R Bl_I(R). Its map to the base blowup is finite. This uses no false unrestricted blowup base-change equality.

Every surviving positive-dimensional source component has generic image outside the base closed point: a component mapping entirely there would be finite over a field and zero-dimensional. A base exceptional effective Cartier equation is a unit away from that point, hence nonzero on each surviving reduced component. Its pullback is therefore regular. Actual effective Cartier constituents pull back effectively, as do their nonnegative real combinations. A contracted proper integral source curve has an integral curve image under the finite map. Viewed over the base residue field, pulled-back bundle degree is the image degree times the finite function-field degree. Intrinsic degree over the source residue field divides this by its positive closed residue degree. Thus nonnegative curve degrees are preserved.

Evaluation also agrees on arbitrary supports: pass first to Frac(B/Q), pull back the invertible lattice with its generic trivialization, and compose its valued centre with the base map. The pulled lattice evaluates to the base function restricted to that semivaluation. No map from a total fraction ring into an unsupported quotient is presumed. This proves core pullback geometrically. Ideal extension, uniform limits and actual decreasing representations then preserve C and D.

For an injection R -> B, G331 gives a compact surjective restriction rho and the exact positive descent theorem rho* K_R = {U in K_B constant on EVERY full rho-fibre}, for K=C,D. This includes conductor-infinite, nonminimal, mixed-zero and partial-bottom cases. For normalization, finite conductor value gives a singleton fibre; infinite conductor value gives exactly the conductor-quotient identification. The finite stratum is open and the infinite stratum closed.

For a noninjection, A=R/ker(R->B) is reduced. Its boundary is the closed exact image {v in X_R: v(ker)=infinity}. The injection A -> B satisfies the preceding descent theorem. Restriction K_R -> K_A preserves the classes by ideal restriction and actual representations, but surjectivity of that restriction is not proved. Outside this image fibres are empty. An envelope or intrinsic product on A cannot silently be substituted for an ambient operator on R.

notes.summary: Raw envelope pullback has an inequality and an exact fibre-admissible identity. Admissible unrestricted equality is equivalent to full fibre constancy.
notes.detailedSummary: For bounded finite obstacles and K=C or D, positive descent identifies the constrained competitor sets. Actual membership transfers for the fibre-admissible envelope. No arbitrary supremum closure, upper-semicontinuous regularization or general envelope existence is assumed.
notes.text:
For K=C or D and a bounded finite obstacle f, define the RAW pointwise envelope P_R^K(f)=sup{u in K_R: u<=f}. A sufficiently negative reference constant is an admissible competitor. The resulting function is finite and nonpositive, but its membership in K or any regularity is not presumed.

For a finite injection with restriction rho, define P_(B,fib)^K(f rho) by restricting the upstairs competitors to those constant on every FULL fibre. By n1 and qualified G331, pullback and positive descent give an order-preserving bijection between this competitor set and the downstairs set. Evaluation at each source point therefore gives

P_(B,fib)^K(f rho)=rho* P_R^K(f), and P_B^K(f rho)>=rho* P_R^K(f).

This uses a proved geometric positivity descent theorem. It does not exchange a supremum with an assumed completion operation.

The fibre-admissible upstairs envelope belongs to K_B exactly when the downstairs envelope belongs to K_R. Pullback proves one direction. In the other, the pointwise identity is fibre constant, so full positive descent applies. Thus existence WITH positivity transfers for this constrained operator.

If the unrestricted upstairs envelope is itself in K_B, unrestricted equality holds exactly when it is constant on every full fibre. Necessity follows because a pullback is fibre constant. For sufficiency, descend the actual upstairs envelope to h in K_R. Surjectivity and its obstacle bound give h<=f, so h is a downstairs competitor. Combine its inequality with the general pullback inequality. A fibre-constant raw supremum whose positivity is unproved cannot be inserted as this competitor.

For a noninjective finite map, the exact fibre-admissible identity uses A=R/ker and f restricted to X_A. Pullback of R competitors still gives the unrestricted inequality. Equality with the envelope on A does not prove equality with the restriction of the envelope on R: that would require a separate extension result.

notes.summary: A continuous-obstacle normalization counterexample has entire upstairs envelope (-1,-2), downstairs value -2 at the shared conductor-infinite point, and exact gap one for C and D.
notes.detailedSummary: The excellent reduced surface R=C[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy) has normalization S=C[x,z]_(x,z) × C[y,z]_(y,z) and conductor (x,y). Every geometric C/D potential on the second regular branch obeys the ordinary-order comparison. This computes both envelopes without an unknown envelope theorem. Fibre maximum is discontinuous, and normalized base change explicitly produces vertical components.
notes.text:
Let k=C, R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy), A1=k[x,z]_(x,z), A2=k[y,z]_(y,z), and T=k[z]_(z). R is excellent by the finite-type-field/localization theorem and reduced because (xy)=(x) intersect (y). It has dimension two.

The map R -> S=A1 × A2 identifies R with A1 times_T A2: a pair with common line residue is a lift of that residue plus xa(x,z) on the first factor and yb(y,z) on the second. Local denominators with nonzero constant lift to units of R. The projections R -> Ai are surjective, so the two idempotents generate S as a finite R-module. Each Ai is normal and has the fraction field of its corresponding component. An element of the total quotient ring integral over R lies in both normal factors. Thus S is exactly the finite normalization.

The conductor is c=(x,y), with cS=xA1 × yA2, R/c=T and S/c=T × T. Indeed an element of R has common residue h in T. Multiplication by (1,0) preserves the fibre-product condition only if h=0; zero residues conversely remain compatible after multiplication by any pair. This also proves R=S times_(S/c) (R/c).

Normalize by a=m=(x,y,z). The entire source boundary is the disjoint union of the FULL sections on A1 and A2, with gauges (x,z) and (y,z). Let w1 kill x and let w2 kill y; both induce ord_z on T. Their common restriction v0 kills (x,y) and gives z value one. Its support is nonminimal, below m, and its conductor value is infinity. The full fibre at v0 consists of precisely these two points: every lift kills the conductor and factors through T, whose normalized centred section is the singleton ord_z. These are the only conductor-infinite points downstairs. At finite conductor value a lift is unique, since a finite-valued c in the conductor gives w(s)=v(cs)-v(c).

On ALL X_R set f(v)=-1-1/v(y), with 1/infinity=0. Since v(m)=1, v(y) is in [1,infinity]. Evaluation into this extended interval is continuous, as is reciprocal at infinity. Therefore f is continuous, finite, and between -2 and -1. Its first-branch pullback is constantly -1; its second-branch pullback is -1-1/w(y). It agrees at the whole identified conductor fibre.

Let o2=ord_(y,z) on A2. This is a valuation because its associated graded ring k[y,z] is a domain; local denominators are units. It is normalized, has both parameter values one, and f rho(o2)=-2. For EVERY w in the second section and proper primary ideal J, put d=ord_(y,z)(J). Since J is contained in (y,z)^d and w((y,z))=1, w(J)>=d=o2(J). Unit ideals satisfy the same inequality. Negative profiles, finite nonnegative real sums, uniform C limits and actual decreasing D limits therefore all satisfy u(w)<=u(o2). This includes extended limits without infinity subtraction.

Consequently EVERY C or D competitor u<=f rho on the second branch is at most -2 everywhere. Constant -2 is admissible and below the obstacle, so that entire branch envelope is exactly -2. The first branch envelope is exactly its constant obstacle -1. The simultaneous tuple is genuinely admissible: the single semilocal ideal J=(x,z) × (y,z)^2 contains (aS)^2 and has negative profile (-1,-2). G331 identifies it with an independently geometric potential. Thus the ENTIRE unrestricted upstairs envelope, for BOTH competitor interpretations, is precisely (-1 on X_A1, -2 on X_A2), and belongs to C_S.

Every downstairs competitor pulls back to a second-branch competitor. Hence its value at v0 is at most -2. The downstairs constant -2 is admissible and lies below f, proving P_R^C(f)(v0)=P_R^D(f)(v0)=-2. At w1 the upstairs envelope is -1, so its difference from the pullback downstairs envelope is exactly ONE. No general envelope positivity or regularization theorem is needed. The downstairs envelope is not claimed constantly -2: the primary ideal (x,y^2,yz,z^2) supplies a competitor with first-branch ordinary-order value -1 and value -2 at v0.

The fibre maximum of the actual tuple (-1,-2) also fails. For second-branch monomial valuations w_M(y)=M, w_M(z)=1, M>=1, the conductor value is finite and the fibre singleton, so that maximum is -2. As M tends to infinity, polynomial evaluation tends to the valuation killing y and giving z value one; local unit denominators retain value zero. Thus w_M tends to w2. At v0 the maximum is -1 because the fibre also contains w1. It is discontinuous. Its second-branch restriction violates u(w2)<=u(o2), so it is not even in D on that branch.

The vertical diagnosis is exact algebra: S tensor_R A1=A1 × T, where T maps through A1/(x); similarly over A2. Fully, S tensor_R S=A1 × T × T × A2, already reduced. The T factors have nonempty centred boundaries but no generic field over the corresponding normal target fraction field. Generic Galois traces ignore them, whereas full conductor descent retains their identified points. This prevents extending a normal-domain maximum argument to all finite injections.

This is a higher-dimensional conductor-INFINITE geometric envelope failure with strictly negative continuous obstacle. It is separate from the known curve mixed-zero literal radial obstruction and continuous-degree-trace obstruction.

notes.summary: General ambient-degree finite projection identifies the geometric product, retaining varying generic ranks, inseparability, exact residue weights, all supports and actual bounded D nets.
notes.detailedSummary: Prime filtration gives every degree-n mixed coefficient, and Artinian centre decomposition gives exact f_q weights. Dense ideal tests identify G345's independently geometric measures. Actual Cartier-cycle projection uses general function-field degree, before Chow quotients. Constant ranks, normalization, towers, gauges, nonpure and lower-dimensional cases are explicit.
notes.text:
Let n=dim R>=1 and p=n-1. For a reduced finite map R -> B define the ambient source measure mu_B^[R](U)=sum_(dim B_q=n) f_q mu_(B_q,aB_q)(U|q), where f_q=[kappa(q):kappa(m)]. Each summand is the independently geometric G345 operator of arity p. Smaller centres contribute zero at ambient degree n, while their points and potentials remain. This is not their intrinsic lower-arity operator.

For each top-dimensional minimal prime P of R put K_P=Frac(R/P), d_P=dim_(K_P)(B tensor_R K_P), and let j_P be the boundary inclusion through the quotient. For bounded u1,...,up in D_R, the proved formula is

rho_* mu_B^[R](rho* u1,...,rho* up) = sum_(dim R/P=n) d_P j_(P,*) mu_(R/P,a(R/P))(j_P* u1,...,j_P* up).

No injection is needed; killed components have d_P=0. The same formula with coefficient one decomposes mu_R.

Proof of every selected coefficient: for primary labels I1,...,Ir and finite R-module M, let H_M be the homogeneous degree-n part of its eventual primary quotient-length polynomial. The qualified G345 kernel supplies these polynomials at arbitrary Noetherian hypotheses. The complete immediate SH17.1.6 and 17.4.2--4 units were independently checked for this application. For an exact sequence, Noetherian homogeneous generation of the multigraded intersection module gives I^s M1 contained in I^s M2 intersect M1 contained in I^(s-c) M1. The exterior quotient polynomials have identical top form. The middle quotient length is the difference of the eventual M2 and M3 polynomials. Squeezing on every positive rational ray proves equality of homogeneous forms and hence H_M2=H_M1+H_M3. Smaller-dimensional modules contribute zero. No coefficient inequality is inferred from polynomial domination.

Take a finite prime filtration of B. Such a filtration exists by successively choosing an element with maximal annihilator, which is prime; Noetherianity terminates the increasing submodule construction. A factor R/Q can have dimension n only if Q is minimal, since a strict smaller prime would extend an n-chain. At a top minimal P, reduced R_P is the field K_P. Localizing the filtration counts exactly its R/P factors, each with length one, so their number is d_P. Thus H_B=sum_P d_P H_(R/P). The finite algebra B tensor_R K_P is a reduced localization of B and a product of finite fields. Its dimension is the sum of their FULL field degrees, including inseparability.

For every primary product L the Artinian algebra B/LB decomposes at its closed centres. Composition series give the exact identity length_R(B/LB)=sum_q f_q length_(B_q)(B_q/LB_q). Comparing ambient degree-n forms proves ALL selected mixed coefficients with their factorial convention, including repetitions and unused labels. Choose p input ideals and one base test ideal J, and divide by input denominators. G345's geometric ideal moments then give the proposed measure identity against v(J), and J=a gives equal finite mass. G331's rational ideal-difference lattice is uniformly dense in ALL real continuous functions on X_R; truncated tests v((g)+a^N)=min(v(g),N) retain nonminimal supports. Hence the Radon measures agree.

Uniform rational approximations extend the equality to C tuples. For bounded D tuples choose their actual decreasing C representations. If the prescribed limits are >=-M, all terms are in [-M,0]. Pullback and quotient restriction give actual representations of known D limits. G345's prescribed-limit bounded net continuity on the finite product of index sets passes the identity to D. Continuous pushforward and finite sums commute with weak limits against fixed continuous tests. No measurable monotone theorem for arbitrary nets or unknown D-limit membership is used.

The geometric calculation is also checked directly. On a common actual base PRIMARY model carrying core divisors and an effective exceptional Cartier test, n1 gives the finite actual source model and regular pulled equations. Each integral top source component maps properly and dominantly to an integral top base component, with equal delta-dimension n and general field degree [L:K_P]. Excellence gives the universally catenary setup, with delta(p)=dim R/p and its finite-type transcendence-degree extension. The complete immediate Stacks 42.26.3 proof yields h_* div(h*s)=[L:K_P] div(s) AS CYCLES, before rational equivalence. Its proof uses norm(g)=g^[L:K_P] for a base rational function; no birational degree-one substitution is made.

Apply complete Stacks 33.45.7 numerical projection to the integral proper closed-fibre primes over the base residue FIELD. Pulled intersections multiply by the residue function-field degree, or vanish when image dimension drops. G345's supported Euler/m-filtration construction retains Cartier thicknesses in mixed characteristic. Degree over the base residue field is f_q times degree over the source residue field. Smaller components cannot supply closed-fibre primes of dimension n-1 on a primary blowup. These actual cycle and numerical identities reproduce precisely the coefficient formula for the independently geometric product; module forms compute it rather than redefine it. Norm/divisor, cohomological and dimension foundations inside the published immediate proofs remain disclosed background.

If d_P=d on all top components, the result is d mu_R. This includes normal-domain generic degree and reduced finite-flat rank d. Normalization has every d_P=1 and recovers its full conductor pushforward, with identified masses added. For varying ranks retain the component sum; no global continuous degree function on singular identified fibres is invented.

In a tower, over K_P write B tensor_R K_P=product_Q L_Q and h_Q=dim_(L_Q)(C tensor_B L_Q). Then d_P(C)=sum_Q [L_Q:K_P]h_Q. Closed residue degrees multiply along centre towers. This is the exact composition rule; constant stage degrees multiply. Under primary change b, t(v)=v_a(b) and T(v)=v/t(v), every source lift has the same t. G345 transport mu_b=T_*[t mu_a], with homogeneously transported inputs, commutes with each summand and pushforward. There is ONE measure factor.

For n=1 the formula is the actual zero-input curve reference measure. For n=0 carriers are empty and measures zero. A lower-dimensional exact image can have zero ambient contribution without having zero intrinsic product. Nonreduced generic lengths are not inserted after reduction.

notes.summary: Normal-domain raw envelopes commute, and one arbitrary upstairs slot satisfies a geometric norm-trace projection formula. Inseparability and all supports are included.
notes.detailedSummary: Full fibres on a finite normal field closure are Galois orbits by G331's full-support coefficient trace. Finite maxima descend positively. Orbit averaging and two valid all-pulled product projections establish the new one-slot identity. Vertical components are not covered by the maximum argument; divisor traces have normalized-primary-model Weil coefficients, without a Cartier-determination claim.
notes.text:
Let A be excellent normal local domain, A -> B a finite domain extension, K=Frac(A), L=Frac(B), d=[L:K]. G331 supplies the coefficient norm trace T_(B/A), with finite kernels eta_v of mass d supported on the FULL restriction fibre. For a boundary-power ideal J, v(N(J))=integral w(J) d eta_v. Its proof uses norm embedding products with generic inseparable lengths and polynomial Gauss minimum after the support quotient. Dense all-support ideal tests give lift independence; extending any fibre point to the common closure gives its positive weight and hence full fibre support. The trace preserves C and actual decreasing D, but that grant alone supplies no product identity.

Choose a finite normal splitting field M/K containing L, including inseparable roots, and its finite integral closure E over A. Its automorphism group G has size [M:K]_sep; its embedding multiplicity is [M:K]/|G|. Every embedding of L extends to an automorphism of M, with equal repetitions. E contains B and G preserves E. G331's full-support norm formula for E/A therefore says EVERY fibre on X_E is a G-orbit, including nonminimal supports.

For p:X_E -> X_B and rho_E:X_E -> X_A, embedding counting gives rho_E* (TU)=(d/|G|) sum_g g* p* U. Also max_g g* p* U belongs to C_E or D_E whenever U belongs to the corresponding source class, is constant on every full fibre over A, and positively descends by G331. Every B fibre point extends to E, so its descended value is exactly M U(v)=max_(rho w=v) U(w). Thus M maps C_B to C_A and D_B to D_A. For U<=f rho, M U<=f and U<=rho* M U. Comparing competitor suprema proves P_B^K(f rho)=rho*P_A^K(f), K=C,D, without assuming either envelope is admissible.

For a reduced finite injection over normal A having EVERY minimal source component dominant, restrict U to each domain quotient, apply this maximum theorem and take the finite maximum downstairs. Every source semivaluation kills a minimal prime, so these quotient fibres cover the full fibre. Vertical components invalidate this argument; n3's A1 × T base change explicitly exhibits the failure.

For n=dim A>=2, bounded U in D_B and bounded u2,...,u_(n-1) in D_A, the new geometric identity is

rho_* mu_B^[A](U,rho*u2,...) = mu_A(TU,u2,...).

Proof: let e=[M:L]. By n4 for E/B, p_*mu_E^[A](p*U,rho_E*u2,...)=e mu_B^[A](U,rho*u2,...), with exact closed residue towers. A-automorphisms of E preserve these ambient measures: ideal quotient lengths are invariant, dense tests identify their measures, and the G345 continuities extend invariance to D. Since rho_E g=rho_E, all orbit-transformed selected slots have equal pushforward. Multilinearity in that ONE slot and the displayed orbit sum give

rho_E* mu_E^[A](rho_E*TU,rho_E*u2,...)=d rho_E* mu_E^[A](p*U,rho_E*u2,...).

The left side is ed mu_A(TU,u2,...) by n4; the right side is de times the proposed source pushforward. Divide by ed. Every input is in the established bounded geometric D domain. This proves operator identification rather than assuming a nonlinear trace/product relation.

For arbitrary reduced B over normal A, sum traces over its dominating minimal domain components. Apply n4's component decomposition to arbitrary source tuples and the preceding identity componentwise. Other minimal components have dimension below n and zero ambient product. This dominating trace has no claimed full support on vertical fibres.

The geometric divisor meaning is precise on the prescribed normalized primary models. At a target exceptional DVR Z, write b_Z=ord_Z(a). Its finite integral closure in L is free of rank d. Reduction modulo the base uniformizer gives sum_(Z'|Z) e_(Z'/Z) f_(Z'/Z)=d. For a source Cartier core D on a common source refinement, trace evaluation at ord_Z/b_Z equals (1/b_Z) sum_(Z'|Z) f_(Z'/Z) ord_(Z')(D). These are exactly proper pushforward Weil coefficients. The norm-order formula has an elementary lattice proof: for integral g, determinant of multiplication on the free integral-closure module has order equal to its cokernel length by Smith normal form; Artinian centre decomposition gives sum f ord(g). Multiply a rational g by a large uniformizer power and subtract its finite norm order to obtain the general case. Further birational refinements preserve the dominating DVR and its coefficient. No finite Cartier determination downstairs, arbitrary-model classification or nonnormal Weil-effectivity substitution is claimed. Positive completed geometry follows from G331 and the product identity just proved.

In finite domain towers with normal targets wherever the traces are used, embedding counts and generic inseparable multiplicities give the unnormalized trace tower identity. Finite sums extend it to actual decreasing D limits. All lifts have the same primary-gauge denominator, so traces obey the homogeneous cocycle and their product identity the one-factor measure law.

notes.summary: Reduced finite-flat maps admit determinant fibre maxima, unrestricted raw envelope equality and a geometric one-slot trace formula. Tracing several arbitrary slots is disproved.
notes.detailedSummary: Finite-free determinant kernels retain nonreduced support fibres and inseparable lengths. Characteristic coefficient ideals, corrected by a sufficiently deep PRIMARY power, express fibre maxima in the geometric class. Actual decreasing nets extend this to D. Normalization base change proves the one-slot product formula; a split rank-two threefold rejects the nonlinear multiple-trace shortcut.
notes.text:
Assume R excellent reduced local and B a nonzero reduced finite flat algebra of rank d, hence finite free. This is the reduced rank. For a semilocal boundary-power ideal J choose finite R-module generators g_i and h=sum T_i g_i. Write det(t1-m_h)=t^d+sum_i(-1)^i c_i(T)t^(d-i), and let C_i(J) be the coefficient ideals. In particular N_fl(J)=C_d(J). Generator substitutions give coefficient containment in both directions, proving independence. If J contains a^N B, include base generators x of a^N redundantly; their pure norm coefficients are x^d. Thus N_fl(J) contains a boundary power and is unit-or-primary.

For a base semivaluation v with support P, pass first to its valued field K_v=Frac(R/P). F=B tensor_R K_v has dimension d and may be NONREDUCED. Split its residue extensions in a finite normal field M/K_v and extend the valuation. F tensor M is a product of Artinian local algebras with residue M. Filtration by maximal-ideal powers makes multiplication by h upper triangular with its residue scalar on every diagonal entry. Its characteristic polynomial is consequently the product of (t-h_j)^(l_j), with the full Artinian lengths l_j and sum l_j=d. This retains fibre nilpotence and inseparability.

The residue homomorphisms followed by the valuation give centred source points w_j. Polynomial Gauss minimum is multiplicative, proved by dividing least coefficients and reducing nonzero residue polynomials. Therefore v(N_fl(J))=sum_j l_j w_j(J). The finite measure eta_v=sum l_j delta_(w_j) is independent of splitting choices: these ideal moments and mass d determine it by G331's dense semilocal ideal-difference lattice. Every full-fibre point occurs for some compatible extension to M; choice independence proves full fibre support. Thus each fibre has at most d points, including all supports. The trace tau U=integral U d eta_v is continuous on continuous functions by dense tests and the fixed mass bound, and maps a rational negative ideal profile to -v(N_fl(J))/q. G331 comparison gives C preservation. Finite positive sums commute with actual decreasing nonpositive limits and give actual C representations, proving D preservation.

A separate argument proves geometric fibre maxima. Put m=min_(rho w=v) w(J), the least Gauss value of the residue roots h_j. Every coefficient c_i has Gauss value at least im. If they were all strictly larger than im, insertion of a root of value m in its monic equation would make the leading term uniquely least-valued, impossible. Hence

min_(rho w=v) w(J)=min_(1<=i<=d) v(C_i(J))/i

on EVERY support, with zero ideals valued infinity. The last norm coefficient is finite and bounds this minimum. Let L=sup_X v(C_d(J))/d, which is finite because C_d contains a boundary power. Choose integer N>dL. Replacing each C_i by C_i+a^N leaves the minimum unchanged, since N/i>L. These are now allowed unit-or-primary ideals. For U=-w(J)/q,

M U(v)=max_(rho w=v) U(w)=max_i[-v(C_i(J)+a^N)/(qi)].

The finite maximum is an allowed rational profile after taking a common denominator and ideal sum. Thus it belongs to the independently geometric C_R through G331. Fibre maximum contracts uniform distances, so rational approximation gives M(C_B) contained in C_R. For an actual decreasing C_B-net, finite fibres and directedness give max U_alpha decreasing to max U: choose one index controlling all finitely many fibre values, using arbitrary finite thresholds for bottom values. This supplies an actual C_R representation and proves M(D_B) contained in D_R, with no increasing closure. The competitor argument of n5 now proves unrestricted RAW envelope equality for reduced finite flat maps over arbitrary reduced excellent targets, including nonnormal targets. Actual membership transfers when known. This flat theorem has its own coefficient proof; it does not assume a false Galois maximum theorem for every injection.

For n=dim R>=2, bounded U in D_B and remaining bounded pulled inputs, the new geometric product identity is

rho_* mu_B^[R](U,rho*u2,...)=mu_R(tau U,u2,...).

Proof: normalize R by finite semilocal S and put B'=B tensor_R S. Flatness makes B -> B' injective. At each normal local centre S_i, B'_i is free of rank d and its generic algebra is the reduced localization B tensor_R Frac(R/P_i). A nilpotent dies generically, and torsion-freeness over the domain forces it to be zero. Thus B' is reduced. Flat going-down shows its minimal components over S_i are all dominant.

Determinant matrices commute with base change. The generator images generate the extended ideal even if tensoring the ideal inclusion itself was not injective. Consequently the pullback of tau U to S_i equals the sum normal-domain trace of U pulled to B'_i, first on rational profiles, then uniformly and by finite-kernel decreasing limits. Apply n5's one-slot identity over each S_i and push along S -> R with G345's exact normalization residue weights. The right side becomes mu_R(tau U,u2,...). The map B -> B' has generic degree ONE on every minimal component of B: normalization becomes K_(P_i) over its contracted minimal prime and changes no source generic field. Apply n4 to that map on the pulled-back source tuple. With the multiplying centre residue degrees, its left side becomes exactly rho_*mu_B^[R](U,rho*u2,...). Lower-dimensional centres have zero ambient degree in both routes but retain all points. This proves the identity with the independently geometric operator.

The trace is therefore an actual downstairs completed geometric function with normalization coefficients equal to the proper Weil pushforward described in n5. No nonnormal Weil divisor is asserted Cartier. Flat trace towers compose: after support-field splitting, flatness makes the first Artinian factor length multiply the second residue-factor lengths, so successive kernels equal the direct kernel.
